stories.title: Trump says he’ll meet with Kim Jong Un before end of year
stories.summary:
President Donald Trump said Wednesday that he expects to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un before the end of the year. The potential summit would mark their fourth face-to-face meeting since Trump’s first term, when the two leaders met in Singapore in 2018 and Vietnam in 2019.

Trump told reporters that Kim had responded positively to his proposal for talks. However, North Korea has denied holding discussions with what it called a “hostile” United States, while praising the personal relationship between the two leaders.

stories.title: Human remains found at Lake Mead National Recreation Area near Las Vegas
stories.summary:
Human remains were discovered at Lake Mead National Recreation Area near Las Vegas after record-low water levels exposed a beach. Visitors reported finding the skeletal material, which prompted an investigation into the site.

According to witnesses and reports from BBC and Washington Times, the remains include what appears to be a human jawbone with teeth still attached. The discovery highlights how extreme drought conditions in the region are uncovering previously submerged areas of the reservoir.

stories.title: Second Ukrainian national arrested over 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blast
stories.summary:
A second Ukrainian national has been arrested in connection with the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline explosions. The suspect was detained in Croatia, marking a significant development in the ongoing investigation into the sabotage of the undersea gas infrastructure.

The arrest comes one year after another Ukrainian man, identified as an ex-army officer, was held and subsequently transferred to Germany for questioning. Authorities are focusing on the roles played by individuals involved in the physical execution of the attack.

According to reports, the newly arrested man is alleged to have been one of the scuba divers who planted explosives on the pipelines during the 2022 incident. The case has drawn international attention due to its geopolitical implications and the complex nature of the underwater sabotage.

stories.title: Judge removed from Karmelo Anthony case as defense seeks retrial in Texas track-meet stabbing
stories.summary:
A Texas judge was removed from the Karmelo Anthony case on Wednesday as his defense team continues to seek a retrial. The move comes after Anthony, now 19, was convicted in June of murdering Austin Metcalf, a 17-year-old athlete, during a high school track meet.

Anthony had been sentenced to 35 years in prison for the fatal stabbing that occurred last April. His attorneys successfully petitioned to have the trial judge excluded from all future appeal efforts related to his conviction.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the action by describing the court as “corrupt and fatally politicized.” He framed the sanctions as a response to what he characterized as institutional corruption within the organization.

The ICC and various world leaders have condemned the U.S. decision. The court’s leadership criticized the move, which marks a significant escalation in tensions between Washington and the international judicial body.

stories.title: In Big Walk, players just walk and talk – and find joy along the way: ‘Some stories we’ve heard are punch-in-the-gut beautiful’
stories.summary:
Melbourne-based studio House House is developing Big Walk, a new title that shifts focus from traditional objectives to simple exploration and conversation. The team, known for Untitled Goose Game, designed the game so players' primary goal is to walk together with friends.

During an interview, the developers took journalists on a hike through local scrubland to demonstrate the game's core philosophy. They traveled by train to the beach and relaxed in sand dunes, mirroring the unhurried pace of Big Walk.

The studio emphasizes that the experience is about finding joy in shared movement rather than completing tasks. Developers describe the stories players share during these walks as "punch-in-the-gut beautiful," highlighting the emotional resonance of casual interaction.

stories.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker – save your family while becoming what you hate
stories.summary:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark fantasy role-playing game developed by some of the talent behind The Witcher 3. It follows Coen, who is human by day and vampire by night, as he navigates difficult choices to save his family.

Set in the 14th century in the fictional land of Vale Sangora, the game takes place in a Carpathian valley of wetlands, mountains, and forests that is cut off from the rest of the world. The region is under the rule of a vicio, creating an isolated and oppressive environment for the protagonist.

The story begins in the 1300s but could span centuries through upcoming sequels, suggesting the start of an epic saga. Players will experience Coen's transformation into what he hates while attempting to protect his loved ones.

stories.title: Did someone wearing Meta Glasses film you today? Are you sure?
stories.summary:
The Guardian reports that Meta Glasses are raising fresh privacy concerns as users describe being secretly filmed in private and public settings. The piece asks whether the popular smartglasses could mark a major shift in personal surveillance.

Interviewees say they have been recorded at home, at concerts, and at work without clear notice. One Los Angeles-based man shared an account of someone expressing intent to record strippers, illustrating how the device’s camera can be used for intrusive purposes.

The article frames the issue as a potential “final nail in the coffin” for privacy, while also noting that many people may not even realize they are being filmed. The reporting relies on anonymous accounts and personal anecdotes rather than formal investigations or legal findings.

stories.title: Claude to start watermarking AI-generated text – but will it make quality worse?
stories.summary:
Anthropic says Claude will begin watermarking AI-generated text as part of its effort to comply with EU regulation. The company plans to change the way the chatbot makes small, random choices when producing language.

The move has raised questions about whether the new approach could degrade writing quality. Readers and commentators already associate machine-generated prose with recurring patterns such as overuse of “delve,” excess em dashes, and repetitive constructions like “it’s not X but Y.” The Guardian frames the issue as a potential trade-off between regulatory compliance and the naturalness of Claude’s output.

stories.title: Damaged protection dike in Mindoro puts Naujan residents at risk
stories.summary:
Provincial authorities in Oriental Mindoro inspected a damaged protection dike in Barangay Arangin on Wednesday after strong currents from the Bagto River destroyed a large portion of the structure. The dike serves as the village’s primary defense against flooding.

The inspection was conducted by provincial officials, including Provincial Engineer Edylou, following reports that the damage has put residents at risk. The Provincial Information Office confirmed the assessment and highlighted the urgent need for repairs to restore flood protection in the area.

stories.summary:
OpenAI has introduced new safeguards following a breach at Hugging Face. The company said the measures are intended to strengthen oversight of its models as they move through development.

The updated protocols include more detailed monitoring during the model development process. OpenAI also emphasized greater focus on alignment and security in post-training stages.

stories.title: Dressmaker – a canvas for the creativity of dream dress design
stories.summary:
Dressmaker is a design game co-created by developer Jonathan Hau-Yoon and his sewing-obsessed partner, Sabrina Becker. The project was inspired by Hau-Yoon's desire to make something as meaningful as the environmental strategy game Terra Nil.

Becker had worn a dress she made herself to an event, which sparked the concept for the new title. According to its lead programmer, Dressmaker has been the most technically challenging project he has ever worked on.

stories.title: Will AI give you the job? Automated hiring tools spark discrimination and secrecy lawsuits
stories.summary:
A growing number of lawsuits are challenging the use of artificial intelligence in employment decisions, raising fresh questions about how companies hire and fire. The legal disputes center on automated hiring tools that applicants say have obscured their chances without clear explanation.

Erin Kistler, a product manager with nearly four years of applications to major employers such as PayPal, Microsoft, and Netflix, describes her résumé disappearing into a “black hole.” Her experience is cited in reporting from The Guardian Technology as part of a broader pattern of discrimination and secrecy claims tied to AI-driven hiring systems.

stories.title: Will the future of gaming be powered by upstart indie developers?
stories.summary:
The Guardian Technology reports that the future of gaming may increasingly depend on upstart indie developers. As major publishers retreat into safer, established bets, a new generation of independents is building an alternative from the ground up.

The article draws a parallel to the 1990s film industry, when independent studios and distributors helped revitalize Hollywood. It suggests that gaming may be undergoing a similar shift, with smaller developers filling gaps left by larger companies focused on lower-risk projects.

stories.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Teens with stronger safeguards
stories.summary:
OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Teens, a version of its chatbot designed specifically for users aged 13 to 17. The company describes the release as targeting the first generation growing up with artificial intelligence.

The teen-specific product includes stronger safeguards than standard versions, with content protections focused on self-harm and sexual conversations. OpenAI noted that teenagers are already using ChatGPT for schoolwork and other questions, prompting the development of a more controlled environment.
